correctness.rationale: Frozen proof reconstructs the mean-zero q-point L4 bound c_q=q-2+1/(q-1) and centered cubic moment m_q=(q-2)/sqrt(q-1), the fourth moment expansion of independent Fourier coordinates, and q>=5 positive mixed-energy remainder. The critical q4 case reduces after v=sqrt(sum (Xj/T)^2) to P(t,v)=3t^4+2t²+1-(8/sqrt3)tv+(2/3)v². Its minimizer is v=2sqrt3 t when t<=1/(2sqrt3), strictly positive, otherwise v=1 with exact factor (sqrt3 t-1)^2(3t²+2sqrt3 t+5)/3; equality forces one axis, then Fourier inversion forces scalar character. Independently verified scalar factorization, 800 sampled q=4 Fourier arrays on 2/3 axes, and exact q=2/3 additive witness moments 21 and 77. The unrestricted q,d claim rests on analytic proof, not finite checks.
residual_risks: The centered complex Lagrange extremum argument and all equality constraints are nonstandard and need retention in final scientific text; sample tests alone insufficient.

value.rationale: Resolving exact previously excluded smallest admissible group order four is a sharp structural endpoint, with complete equality rigidity for arbitrary number of coordinate axes. The discrete threshold distinguishes q>=4 from explicit q2/3 failures and makes the result useful in finite-group Fourier extension.
residual_risks: Quantitative stability remainder is proved only q>=5; none asserted at q4.

final_claim: For any finite abelian H with q=|H|>=4 and any d>=2, Fourier synthesis supported on the union of d coordinate axes in H^d has sharp normalized fourth moment E|F|^4 <= q (sum |a|²)^2, with equality only for a scalar character on one whole axis; q=2,3 violate the bound, and q>=5 admits a positive pairwise energy-spread remainder.
limitations: Only fourth moments, uniform dual probability, equal base group along all axes.
No assertion of optimal q2 or q3 constants.
